breakpoints.note: gnutls_pkcs12_import successfully parses the 13-byte crafted DER input as a PKCS12 structure (returns >= 0), allowing execution to proceed to gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse which eventually calls _decode_pkcs12_auth_safe where the vulnerability is triggered.

Reads the attacker-controlled contentType OID from the parsed PKCS12 ASN.1 structure into the stack-allocated oid buffer. For the crafted input containing a minimal single-byte OID (0x20), asn1_read_value returns ASN1_SUCCESS and writes a short value to oid without null-terminating the buffer, leaving bytes from offset 5 onward uninitialized.

The 128-byte stack buffer oid is declared without initialization. The code at line 59 reserves one byte for null-termination (len = sizeof(oid) - 1) but never writes oid[len] = '\0' after asn1_read_value fills the buffer. When asn1_read_value writes data without null-termination for an edge-case OID input, the remaining bytes stay uninitialized and are read by the subsequent strcmp call.

strcmp reads oid which has 5 initialized bytes at offsets 0-4 followed by uninitialized stack memory. Since oid is not null-terminated after the initialized portion, strcmp reads past it into uninitialized bytes at offset 5. MSan detects use-of-uninitialized-value at this comparison against DATA_OID ("1.2.840.113549.1.7.1", 21 bytes including null).
